output.summary: Digital Design Communications will test the fire and intrusion alarm devices on the second floor of the Lincoln Elementary School building. The company will also find which devices were affected by the demolition work and troubleshoot other devices that are not working. This is part of the school's water intrusion repairs and window replacement project, with work scheduled from January 25 to March 15, 2024.

output.summary: The board approves a second amendment to the contract with HERTZ Environmental, Inc. to continue closing out the Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan for the Claremont Middle School Multipurpose Room and Kitchen Project. output.summary: The board approves a first amendment to the contract with ACC Environmental Consultants, Inc. for the Roosevelt Middle School Modernization Project. The text does not describe the services.

output.headline: Awards Data Media Services $119,000 to install door intercom systems at five school sites
output.summary: Data Media Services will install AIPhone door entry intercom systems at Thornhill Elementary School, Oakland Academy of Knowledge, Lockwood Steam Academy, Lockwood CDC and Kaiser Early Childhood Center. The $119,000 price includes a $14,000 contingency (a cushion for unexpected costs). The company was the lowest qualified bidder, and work is expected from January 25 to April 23, 2024.

output.headline: Awards Data Media Services $123,000 to install door intercom systems at five school sites
output.summary: Data Media Services will install AIPhone door entry intercom systems at Oakland Tech Upper Campus, Montera Middle School, Jefferson CDC, Hillcrest Elementary School and Bella Vista CDC. The $123,000 price includes a $15,000 contingency (a cushion for unexpected costs). The company was the lowest qualified bidder, and work is expected from January 25 to April 23, 2024.

output.headline: Pays Jensen Hughes up to $33,880 to review fire alarm design at the Santa Fe Campus therapy unit
schools: Child Care Services Medical Therapy Unit at Santa Fe Campus
output.summary: Jensen Hughes will consult on the fire alarm design for the Child Care Services Medical Therapy Unit at Santa Fe Campus. It will check that the design meets state building and fire codes and district design standards, join meetings, and watch testing of the fire and intrusion alarms. The limit of $33,880 includes up to $3,080 for additional services, and work is scheduled from January 25 to December 31, 2024.

output.headline: Awards KM 106 Construction $462,000 to replace play structures and add nature areas at Manzanita Elementary
output.summary: KM 106 Construction will tear out the existing play structures, safety matting and asphalt at Manzanita Elementary School. It will then install new play matting tiles and nature exploration areas. The $462,000 price includes a $29,000 contingency (a cushion for unexpected costs). The company was the lowest qualified bidder, and work is expected from January 25 to April 23, 2024.

output.headline: Awards Redgwick Construction $463,100 to build a nature exploration area at Bella Vista Elementary
output.summary: Redgwick Construction will remove old play structures, matting and an asphalt layer at Bella Vista Elementary School, move a seating area, and install a new nature exploration area of about 3,000 square feet. The $463,100 price includes a $35,000 contingency allowance (a cushion for unexpected costs). The company was the lowest qualified bidder, and work is expected from January 25 to April 23, 2024.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $50,000 for a contractor to manage district and citywide safety planning

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $50,000.00

output.summary: The board approves, after work began on December 11, 2023, a services agreement with an individual contractor for project management of district and citywide safety planning. The work includes a charter and labor working group, monthly safety communications, and aligning the district's safety planning efforts. The agreement runs through June 30, 2024 and may not exceed $50,000.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $31,757 for SEE Change Consulting's school climate review and staff coaching
output.summary: SEE Change Consulting would assess school climate and culture, train all employees in communication skills, coach the leadership team, and facilitate dialogue for adults in unproductive conflict. The work runs December 18, 2023 through June 28, 2024, so this ratification comes after the work began. The cost is capped at $31,757.

output.headline: Lets The Watershed Project add a rainwater cistern, trees and a mural at Coliseum College Prep at no cost
output.summary: This is a no-cost agreement (a memorandum of understanding) that lets The Watershed Project install a rainwater tank, new California native trees with irrigation, redwood benches and a planter, and a mural at Coliseum College Preparatory Academy. The district agrees to maintain the plantings and other installations, and The Watershed Project will keep the rainwater system in good condition with yearly campus check-ups. The agreement runs from December 1, 2023 through December 31, 2034.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $19,003.80 for Wellness Together counseling at Crocker Highlands Elementary
output.summary: Wellness Together would provide school-based counseling services to participating students at Crocker Highlands Elementary School, including individual and group sessions and referrals to community mental health providers. The agreement runs August 14, 2023 through May 29, 2024, so this ratification comes after the work began. The cost is capped at $19,003.80.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $6,688.50 for N2Y training webinars for special education staff
output.summary: N2Y LLC would provide onsite professional learning and six hours of targeted live webinars for the Special Education Department. The agreement runs July 10, 2023 through June 30, 2024, so this ratification comes after the work began. The cost is capped at $6,688.50.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $60,000 for Seneca Family of Agencies student support at Horace Mann after-school
output.summary: Seneca Family of Agencies would provide a Student Support Assistant five days a week during After School Program hours at Horace Mann Elementary School, giving instructional, therapeutic and behavioral support to students and staff. The agreement runs January 8, 2024 through May 23, 2024, so this ratification comes after the work began. The cost is capped at $60,000.

output.headline: Pays Blenderbox up to $1,455,000 to configure the EnrollWise enrollment platform through June 2024
output.summary: Blenderbox will set up its EnrollWise platform, which the Student Assignment Center already uses, to take applications and offers for the district's Summer Learning Programs. It will also make one-time upgrades for early childhood and Student Assignment Center admissions and update student eligibility and priority rules to follow new policies. The service period is December 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024, which began before the board vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $780 for HeartStart CPR to teach a CPR and First Aid class at Redwood Heights
output.summary: HeartStart CPR would teach a three-hour CPR and First Aid class to thirty teachers at Redwood Heights Elementary School. The agreement runs December 12, 2023 through May 24, 2024, so this ratification comes after the work began. The cost is capped at $780.

output.headline: Approves up to $101,490 for Quattrocchi Kwok Architects' design work at six high schools
output.summary: Quattrocchi Kwok Architects would prepare electrical, plumbing, architectural and mechanical drawings and construction documents that can be used for bidding, and oversee construction, at Oakland High, Skyline High, Madison Park Academy, Castlemont High, Oakland Technical High and Fremont High. The agreement period began September 7, 2023 and runs through June 30, 2024, before this vote. The cost is capped at $101,490.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $50,000 for Khepera Curriculum Group to support Manhood Development Program instructors
output.summary: Khepera Curriculum Group would support the Office of Equity's African American Male Achievement leadership in training and developing instructors for the Manhood Development Program at 15 to 20 school sites. It would also help run the instructors' professional learning community and provide access to its curriculum outline. The agreement runs December 15, 2023 through May 31, 2024, so this ratification comes after the work began. The cost is capped at $50,000.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $20,000 for Flourish Agenda to support Hoover Elementary's family council
output.summary: Flourish Agenda would facilitate monthly Family Council meetings at Hoover Elementary School, introduce a parent leadership framework, help the council set family engagement goals, and write a report with recommendations for next year. The agreement runs September 1, 2023 through May 31, 2024, so this ratification comes after the work began. The cost is capped at $20,000.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost Living Jazz choir rehearsal for the MLK Tribute concert
output.summary: Living Jazz teaching artists would lead a rehearsal on January 11, 2024 for a united choir of 2nd and 3rd graders from Glenview, Cleveland, Carl B Munck and La Escuelita schools. It prepares them for the MLK Tribute concert at the Paramount Theater on January 13, 2024. The district pays nothing, and this ratification comes after the rehearsal date.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $3,000 for The SIFE Equity Project to review reading support at Oakland International High
output.summary: The SIFE Equity Project would work with a teacher at Oakland International High School to review how the reading program supports student growth, meeting twice a month to look at data and set entrance and exit criteria. The agreement runs December 1, 2023 through May 15, 2024, so this ratification comes after the work began. The cost is capped at $3,000.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $4,966 for Bureau of Education Research staff well-being training at Bunche Academy
output.summary: Bureau of Education Research would present strategies to educators at Ralph J. Bunche Academy on mental and emotional tools that support learning and the well-being of students, staff and school culture. The training was set for one day, November 17, 2023, so this ratification comes after it. The cost is capped at $4,966.

output.headline: Adds $19,030 to Yeah, Art! music classes, now also at Melrose Leadership Academy
output.summary: This amendment adds $19,030 to the contract with Yeah, Art! for music production, vocal and instrument classes, raising the cap from $28,000 to $47,030. The classes continue at Roosevelt Middle School and are added at Melrose Leadership Academy, for up to 30 students per class, 2 days a week. The term is unchanged (July 26, 2023 through May 23, 2024), so this ratification comes after the term began.

output.headline: Adds $5,000 to a mental health intern supervision contract, raising the cap to $14,360

money.evidence: $5,000.00, increasing the not to exceed amount of the Agreement from $9,360.00 to $14,360.00

output.summary: This amendment adds 38 hours and $5,000 to a contract for an individual to supervise graduate social work and family therapy interns who fill gaps in mental health services. The cap rises from $9,360 to $14,360. The term is unchanged (September 1, 2023 through May 31, 2024), so this ratification comes after the term began.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $5,000 for NCAOSA music and dance teacher training
output.summary: NCAOSA would provide a professional learning program for 26 to 30 district music and dance teachers, with more than 60 hours of hands-on learning and curriculum design led by presenters from the American Orff-Schulwerk Association. It supports the district's goal of providing arts to every OUSD elementary student. The agreement runs August 1, 2023 through June 28, 2024, so this ratification comes after the work began. The cost is capped at $5,000.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $12,500 for Reading Partners one-on-one reading help at Lockwood STEAM Academy
output.summary: Reading Partners would give about forty students chosen by staff a one-on-one reading intervention twice a week at Lockwood STEAM Academy. The goal is for participating students to improve their reading rate by 70% to 90% by the final evaluation. The agreement runs August 7, 2023 through June 30, 2024, so this ratification comes after the work began. The cost is capped at $12,500.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $3,700 for Kimochis training for early childhood special education teachers
output.summary: Kimochis/Plushy Feely Corporation would lead a one-day training at Burbank Preschool on January 8 for about 50 Early Childhood Special Education teachers and K-2 mild-moderate self-contained class teachers. It covers the Kimochis social-emotional curriculum and how to adapt it for students with special needs. The agreement period began December 11, 2023, so this ratification comes after the training date. The cost is capped at $3,700.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost Northeastern University partnership to train OUSD library leaders
output.summary: Northeastern University - Mills College Campus, Lead by Learning would support the district's Library Leadership Team with goal-setting, monthly leader meetings and planning for staff development on building inclusive library spaces. Results are to be measured with agendas and surveys. The agreement runs August 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024 at no cost to the district, and this ratification comes after it began.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $109,000 for Sown To Grow's social-emotional learning program and software
output.summary: The board is approving, after the fact, an agreement with Sown To Grow to help carry out its program for fall 2023. It includes emotional check-ins, a social-emotional learning (SEL) screener and curriculum, software licenses for teachers, students and administrators, training and coaching, and reports on student well-being. The service period is August 1, 2023 through February 29, 2024, and it began before the board vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $55,000 for UC Berkeley research on OTR residents and a student data-sharing agreement
output.summary: The University of California, Berkeley campus will carry out a qualitative research study with OTR Residents, graduates and people who have left the program. The agreement also includes a data-sharing agreement setting terms for how the district shares student data with the university and how the university protects it. The service period of February 22 through June 30, 2023 ended before this January 2024 board vote.

output.summary: Destiny Arts Center would provide movement and performing arts programming at Westlake Middle School for the Spring 2024 semester, including teaching artists with training and supervision. output.headline: Ratifies up to $5,200 for Evolve Coaching & Consulting leadership coaching for Network 2
output.summary: Evolve Coaching & Consulting would provide one-on-one leadership coaching for Network 2, with two 60-minute sessions per month for six months and two optional supervisor sessions. The agreement runs January 8, 2024 through June 30, 2024, so this ratification comes after the work began. The cost is capped at $5,200.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $50,000 for Fam 1st Family Foundation to run the Oakland Athletic League media team
output.summary: Fam 1st Family Foundation would coordinate media coverage of middle and high school athletics for the Oakland Athletic League, train students twice a week in media, graphic design, journalism, photography and video editing, and offer internships to high school students. The agreement runs January 1, 2024 through December 30, 2024, so this ratification comes after the term began. The cost is capped at $50,000.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $13,000 for Lead Liberated leadership coaching at Hoover Elementary
output.summary: Lead Liberated would provide leadership coaching in two parts to the principal and a member of the school's leadership team at Hoover Elementary School, aimed at identifying and interrupting racism in their leadership practices. The agreement runs September 1, 2023 through May 31, 2024, so this ratification comes after the work began. The cost is capped at $13,000.

output.headline: Applies to renew state preschool and family literacy funding for 2024-25; amount set by the state
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution approving the district's application to renew state funding for its State Preschool Program and its Pre-Kindergarten and Family Literacy Program, both run by the Early Childhood Education Department. The funding amount will be decided by the California Department of Education. The resolution also authorizes who may sign for the district.

output.headline: Approves no-cost University of San Francisco Upward Bound advising and student data sharing
output.summary: The University of San Francisco's Upward Bound Project would provide advisors to help OUSD staff support students with planning after high school, at no cost to the district. A paired data sharing agreement (DSA) sets the terms for sharing student data with the university, including view-only access to Aeries and other student data, and for protecting it. Both run July 1, 2023 through August 31, 2024, so they began before this vote.

output.headline: Approves $281,369,616.93 in district bill payments from June to December 2023
output.summary: The board approves a report of 7,521 accounts payable checks, which the district has already printed to pay vendors and other bills, totaling $281,369,616.93. The payments were made from June 1, 2023 through December 31, 2023, covering June 2023 at the end of fiscal year 2022-23 and the first half of 2023-24. They are listed in Exhibit 1.

output.headline: Lets Masri Investment Corporation test soil and groundwater at Westlake Middle School at no cost
output.summary: The board approves a license letting Masri Investment Corporation enter parts of Westlake Middle School to investigate soil, soil gas and groundwater. The San Francisco Bay Regional Water Quality Control Board requested the work. The access lasts through September 30, 2024 or until the work is done, and costs the district nothing.

output.headline: Approves $39,115,840.55 in district bill payments made in April 2022
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title and text say Fiscal Year 2022-2023 and 'As of April 30, 2022', but April 2022 falls in fiscal year 2021-2022 (July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2022).
output.summary: The board approves a report of 1,391 accounts payable checks, which the district has already printed to pay vendors and other bills, totaling $39,115,840.55. The payments were made from April 1, 2022 through April 30, 2022, and are listed in Exhibit 1. The title and text call this fiscal year 2022-2023, although April 2022 falls in 2021-22.

output.headline: Approves $142,135,514.49 in district payroll for July to December 2023
output.summary: The board approves a payroll report covering 5,508 printed payroll checks and 47,621 direct deposits, totaling $142,135,514.49. The payments were made from July 1, 2023 through December 31, 2023, the first half of fiscal year 2023-24, and are listed in Exhibit 1.

output.headline: Adopts a resolution allowing temporary borrowing between district funds for 2023-24
output.summary: The board adopts Resolution No. 2324-0137, which covers temporary borrowing between district funds for fiscal year 2023-24. The text does not state any dollar amount or the terms of the borrowing.

output.headline: Approves the minutes of the board's January 8, 2024 annual organizational meeting
output.summary: The board ratifies the written minutes of its Annual Organizational Meeting held on January 8, 2024. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting. This is a record-keeping item with no cost.

output.headline: Approves the minutes of the board's January 8, 2024 special meeting
output.summary: The board ratifies the written minutes of its Special Meeting held on January 8, 2024. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting. This is a record-keeping item with no cost.

output.headline: Approves the minutes of the board's January 10, 2024 regular meeting
output.summary: The board ratifies the written minutes of its Regular Meeting held on January 10, 2024. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting. This is a record-keeping item with no cost.

output.headline: Pays Teach for America up to $250,000 to recruit and coach new teachers, July 2024 to June 2026
output.summary: Teach for America will make reasonable efforts to recruit teachers from a range of academic majors and career fields, select them for its program, and present them to the district for employment. It will also provide instructional coaching for selected new hires. The agreement runs for two school years, from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2026, at a cost of up to $250,000.

output.headline: Cuts the Audit Committee from seven members to five starting February 1, 2024
output.summary: The board amends Bylaw 9131, which covers advisory and oversight committees, to reduce the Audit Committee's membership from seven to five members. The change takes effect February 1, 2024. It has no stated cost.

output.headline: Approves Measure G1 grant changes for Frick United Academy and carryover requests for two schools
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution following the Measure G1 oversight commission's recommendation. It approves an amended 2023-2024 grant proposal for Frick United Academy of Language. It also approves requests to carry over and spend 2022-2023 Measure G1 funds at Frick United Academy of Language and Oakland Charter Academy. The text does not state dollar amounts.

output.headline: Names members to open seats on the Career Technical Education Advisory Committee
output.summary: The board adopts Resolution No. 2324-0170, which names members to fill some vacancies on the Career Technical Education Advisory Committee and sets their terms. The text does not list the members or the term dates.

output.headline: Appoints three members to the Measures N and H College and Career Readiness Commission
output.summary: The board ratifies the Board President's appointment of one new member and reappointment of two members to the Measures N and H College and Career Readiness Commission. One of the reappointed members will serve as Chair. Terms run from February 1, 2024 through January 31, 2026.

output.headline: Reappoints two Audit Committee members for terms running February 2024 through January 2026
output.summary: The board ratifies the Board President's reappointment of two members to the Audit Committee: one for a third term and one for a second term. Both are described as having given satisfactory service. The new terms run from February 1, 2024 through January 31, 2026.

output.headline: Approves the 2024-2025 school-year academic calendar for transitional kindergarten through 12th grade
output.summary: The board approves the draft 2024-2025 academic calendar for transitional kindergarten through 12th grade as the district's official calendar for that school year. The text does not list the dates.
